speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
James: Do you want to start us off?
Great performance. Brentford had 37  crosses—you must be really proud of  
the defending, particularly in their own box?
Yeah, um, it’s a difficult place  to come, a difficult place to win,  
but also a difficult place to keep  them out because, as you said,  
the way they play and the way they set up, you  have to defend your box no matter how you play.
You know, they’re getting throw-ins into  the box, set-pieces, crosses—you’re just  
going to have to deal with that irrespective  of how you want to tactically approach it.
And I just thought the lads handled that awfully  well. We knew we had to. It was going to be  
about nullifying their threats.  And, yeah, the lads were brilliant.
We always felt we had the quality in  our football to hurt them the other  
way. Our second goal was outstanding,  and we were always a threat when we had  
the ball. So, yeah, credit to the boys. Did it feel great to get that result?
Yeah, great. You know, great  for the supporters and great  
for the players too because they’re all hurting.
You know, the players are hurting as well,  and I’m sure—I know—the supporters are.  
It’s not where they want to see their team,  and it’s certainly not where we want to be.
We need to rectify that. But, yeah, it was  great to see that we could enjoy this game,  
enjoy the result, and get the rewards for  it—for both the players and the supporters.
And we need to—you know—it’s only one game.  We need to rectify our league position. We  
know that. We’re nowhere near where we  want to be. It’s been disappointing,  
but not through a lack of effort, will,  or determination from the players.
They’re giving everything. And I was  super pleased today that they could share  
that moment with the supporters. What’s the latest with signings?
Yeah, great to get Kevin in. You know,  we desperately needed a defender.
But, yeah, getting him is great because he’s a  great fit for us. You know, he’s had a strong  
career, but he’s at an age now where he really  wants to kick on. He’s got all the attributes  
we look for—he’s really strong one-on-one, he’s  quick, he’s dynamic, he wants to play on the ball.
And, like I said, he’s just at  a stage in his career where he’s  
really determined to kick on now and  make an impact. So, really pleased.
I think it’ll be a lift for the whole group.
With Richy, we’ll probably have more  information tomorrow. It doesn’t look good,  
but I think he’s seeing a specialist tomorrow,  and we’ll have more information then. 
With the deadline tomorrow, do  you expect the club to be busy?
Look, I think the club is still  looking for opportunities.
You know, I think, yeah, I’ve been saying for  a long time they’ve been working hard. And, you  
know, we just don’t want to bring just anyone in,  and sometimes that takes a bit longer, which is  
frustrating for everybody—I guess it’s frustrating  for the club, for the players, and for me.
But I’m really pleased we got Kevin in  because he’s a good fit. And if we can  
find another one, that’d be great. How important was this result?
I guess in the context of where we are in the  season, yeah, it’s an important one because, like  
I said, our league position is not good enough.  We need to address that. We need to improve.
But it’s still the same group of players playing  
Thursday-Sunday. You can’t  get away from that fact.
People can dismiss it, but playing  Thursday-Sunday consistently without  
being able to rotate takes its toll. The  Premier League is a relentless competition.
You’re meeting teams that have had a six-day  break, and we’ve had literally 48 hours sometimes.
From that perspective, I think the pleasing thing  is that we got Micky back on Thursday night,  
we got Jed back in today, and signing  Kevin—at least the group now is getting  
some encouragement and energy from  the fact they’re getting some help.
I’ve got no doubt that will assist us in  addressing our position in the league.
And, you know, we’ve got some massive  opportunities in the back half of the year.
So, important because we have to  improve in the league—there’s no  
doubt about that. Where we are is not good enough.
But I think it was also significant because it was  again done by the same group of players that we’ve  
been asking to do this for quite a while now. Any more signings?
Look, I think, again, it’s about seeing where  we’re at in terms of the fit of the player.
It’s not just about bringing another  body in. I’ve said that all along.
We’re still a little bit thin defensively.
I mean, he goes under the radar, but the  job Archie Gray is doing is just ridiculous.
He’s 18 years old. He’s never played center-back  
before, and he’s playing in the Premier  League and Europe, midweek, every game.
It’s just incredible what he’s churning out.
And Ben’s been brilliant, but  really, at the moment, you know,  
we’ve got to be careful with Micky  because he’s been out for a while.
Getting him back is great, but, you know,  Cristian—we feel he’s still a little bit away.
So, again, if the right opportunity  exists, we’ll go for it. 
You’ve spoken about fatigue—how tough has it been?
Look, how do I say this without repeating  myself or making it sound like an excuse?
It’s very difficult for a group of players to  play Thursday-Sunday and maintain energy levels.
What they’re doing is giving maximum effort.
And maximum effort in a game like today  means that you can’t be sharp and really  
dynamic with and without the  ball. It’s just impossible.
They’re human beings—they’re not robots.
People want to dismiss it. They want to  talk about excuses. But that’s the reality.
I know the reality. These  guys are giving everything.
We knew today wasn’t going to be a game where we  could go out and dominate because Brentford had a  
week to prepare, and we had 50-something  hours with the same group of players.
So, with that context, I think  the performance was outstanding.
Micky—was there a setback, or was it planned?
No, no, no. It’s like I said before the game—he  
played 45 minutes. The plan was  maybe to play him 45 again today.
But then we had to think about it.
I spoke to Micky as well, and I  thought, I’d rather he has another  
full week of training and gets ready for  Thursday night—it’s a big game for us.
We had Jed back today, which gave me  some comfort that we could cover for him.
But, you know, he was never going  to play more than 45 minutes today.
And I just felt, after discussing it with the  medical team and with Micky—who is desperate to  
play—I just think we’ve got to be really smart  about how we integrate him back into the team.
And, obviously, Thursday night is a big game for  
us. Having a week of training will  hopefully get him ready for that.
Any updates on transfers?
Al, I’ve been busy for the last couple of hours,  mate, so I’m not really sure what’s going on.
I’ll check my phone when I get back in the rooms. You must be pleased to have Jed Spence back in  
the team?
Yeah, he’s been outstanding  since he’s come into the team.
He had to bide his time, it’s fair to  say. We needed Jed to really be patient,  
but also just mature a little  bit. And I think he has.
Once he got into the team, he’s looked fantastic.
He was important for us today, and I think  we missed him in the last couple of games.
He’s one of these defenders that  loves the challenge of taking on  
the elite Premier League wingers,  and there are some outstanding ones.
And Bryan Mbeumo—especially here—is right up  there. You could see he loves that challenge.
That’s another reason we kept Micky on ice,  
knowing Jed was back in—it was  going to help us enormously.
Yeah, so I’m really pleased  to get him back into the team.
He’ll be important for us until Destiny  [Udogie] gets back. He’ll be crucial for  
us in this period. What do you make of Archie  Gray? Do you see him playing in another position?
Who knows?
But you can’t lose sight of the fact  that he’s never played there before.
I just think he’s a fantastic player.
I’m so pleased he’s at this football club. He’s  a fantastic kid as well—he just wants to learn.
No task is too much for him.
He tackles everything with a real kind  of calmness that belies his years.
He wants to learn, he wants to get better.
We’re just very, very fortunate  to have him at this football club.
And whatever position he ends up playing,  he’s going to be outstanding because he  
has that attitude of wanting to  improve, wanting to get better.
He’s already set a high benchmark.
There aren’t many 18-year-olds you can throw  into the Premier League, play them out of  
position in such an important area of the  pitch, and see them handle it the way he has.
Just brilliant. That’s everything—thank you, Ange.
Cheers, guys.
title: Brentford 0-2 Tottenham | FULL Ange Postecoglou Post Match Press Conference
